```shiploop-state
{
  "evidence_refs": ["Original request, S1–S2", "Exercise instructions and environment context"],
  "headline": "Intake established the CLI and test outcomes, boundaries, and defaults for unattended delivery.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "summary": "S1 — Fact: The outcome is a Python command-line tool that reads sales CSV files and prints total revenue, revenue by region, and units by product. Fact: The named target grants delivery to the repository and its command-line entry point; its consumer is the person running the tool. Assumption: In the absence of a supplied CSV contract, use header fields region, product, units, and revenue, treat revenue as the row total, aggregate across input files, and use decimal arithmetic for revenue. Open decision — recorded default answers the CSV contract; discovery must first look for an existing contract or sample records, and the decision blocks parsing and aggregation until resolved. Assumption: Invalid input produces a clear error and a nonzero exit status. Open decision — recorded default answers error handling; discovery must first establish any existing input requirements, and the decision blocks finalizing error behavior until resolved. Fact: Discovery has no named team, channel, internal site, document, private repository, owner, or ambiguous business term supplied as a source hint; the workspace and any available sales-record examples are leads, not verified sources. Sensitive locators belong only in an authorized private store, never in committed KNOWLEDGE/. Fact: This is a command-line batch tool, with no interactive shared-session requirements stated; assumption: the local runtime identifies the invoking user, and no shared state, persistence, or cross-user visibility is required. Open decision — recorded default answers runtime and state behavior; discovery must first establish what the runtime already provides and whether any shared state or hidden data is required, and the decision blocks any such interaction design. S2 — Fact: Add tests covering the requested summaries and relevant input behavior; assumption: use Python's standard unittest framework unless discovery establishes a repository convention. Open decision — recorded default answers the test framework; discovery must first establish available tooling and conventions, and the decision blocks choosing the test entry point until resolved. Fact: The repository is empty, this run is unattended, and intake implements nothing; no prior-run continuation is specified. Fact: The isolated source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return; after implementation and final return, the tool and tests must be usable in the returned repository, with summaries visible when the CLI runs and test results visible when tests run. No deployed target is named; an outcome in any deployed target would be visible only after release."
}
```
